meta.unit: bytes-level canonical-quantity gate on ReportedHeader's number and timestamp decode (ReportedHeader.UnmarshalJSON -> strictNumber/strictTime -> checkCanonicalQuantity) — an empty or non-canonical JSON quantity can never become a value
meta.purpose: Task 9 wave 7 brief's mutation requirement: the empty-rejection arm PER WRAPPED FIELD (W7M1 number, W7M2 timestamp — each bypasses its field's canon gate entirely, restoring Codex round 6's finding for that field: v1.13.0 hexutil decodes "" as zero, so "number":"" passes HeadFrom as height 0 and "timestamp":"" passes presence as the Unix epoch), plus the shared canon's arms (W7M3 empty, W7M4 uppercase, W7M5 leading zeros, W7M6 "0x" with no digits). Run through the wave-16 committed applier (.superpowers/sdd/wave16-mutations/mutate.py): exactly-one-occurrence asserted per edit, byte-level backups, in-memory restores verified byte-identical. chain.go is CRLF in the working tree, so multi-line patterns embed \r\n explicitly.
design_notes: EVERY MUTANT LIVES IN THE WAVE-7 CANON GATE — the strict wrappers' gate calls and checkCanonicalQuantity's arms, the single bytes-level enforcement site. The fake-seam tests are STRUCTURALLY BLIND to all six by design: they script *ReportedHeader VALUES above the decode, so every kill here must come from the raw-JSON fixture layer (chain_rawjson_test.go), which drives the REAL stack Dial -> rpc.Client -> ReportedHeader.UnmarshalJSON -> wrappers -> gate. The transcript's kill lists are the proof that layer actually reaches the wrappers.

W7M1 AND W7M2 ARE THE BRIEF'S BINDING PAIR (the empty-rejection arm per wrapped field; property: an empty quantity can never become a value) AND ARE BEHAVIORAL KILLS: under each, the empty-quantity read SUCCEEDS — W7M1 hands HeadFrom a height-0 head from the malformed primary (token 0, Head.Number 0, no rotation), W7M2 hands HeaderTime the Unix epoch — exactly the F2 failover-stopping class the round-6 finding named. The binding regression tests assert error-plus-rotation-plus-landing, so the mutants die on every leg.

W7M4 IS BEHAVIORAL: uppercase digits are a form the pinned hexutil ACCEPTS as a value ("0x5A" decodes to 90), so with the lowercase arm relaxed the matrix's uppercase arms SUCCEED where they assert refusal — for the number field the response even passes the wave-6 exact-height gate (90 == asked 90), proving the canon gate is the ONLY line refusing this form.

W7M3, W7M5 AND W7M6 ARE MESSAGE-LEVEL KILLS, disclosed: the bytes each arm rejects are still refused after the mutation — "" by the next canon arm (the 0x-prefix check), "0x05a" by hexutil's own ErrLeadingZero, "0x" by hexutil's ErrEmptyNumber — so rotation is identical either way and the observable is the violation's NAME. That name is the property: the matrix pins the canon gate's marker ('not a canonical JSON-RPC quantity') and per-arm reason on every refusal, because a gate whose rejections silently devolve to the library's own leniency profile is one library upgrade away from re-admitting the class ("" -> 0 IS that library's current profile one form over). W7M5 subtlety: hexutil's leading-zero message happens to contain the words 'leading zero digits', so that kill rides the canon-marker assertion, not the reason assertion.

MUTANT COMPILABILITY was checked by construction: W7M1/W7M2 leave a bare delegation to the hexutil decoder (no unused variables); W7M3/W7M5/W7M6 delete arms whose operands remain used by later arms; W7M4 widens one condition in place.

SOLVENT_LIVE_RPC_TESTS stays UNSET for every mutation run (no public-endpoint hammering inside a loop; the raw-JSON layer needs no gate — its JSON-RPC servers are local httptest instances). TEST_DATABASE_URL points at solvent_t9w1, never at the backfill daemon's DB.
